title: Wiring of premises
summary: In short: the SA rulebook for low-voltage installations. A certificate of compliance is judged against it.
tip: Why it matters for us: if a joint, gland, or protection choice feels clever, check this before the board is closed.

title: Small-scale embedded generation
summary: In short: extra wiring rules when a small generator, PV included, sits on a normal premises supply.
tip: Why it matters for us: the PV job is part of the premises wiring, not a side project with its own habits.

title: Medium-voltage installations
summary: In short: the wiring code for medium-voltage premises, not the low-voltage board we usually build.
tip: Why it matters for us: a site with an MV intake is a different job. Don't stretch the LV rules up to it.

title: Utility interface
summary: In short: how a small embedded generator is allowed to meet the utility at the point of connection.
tip: Why it matters for us: don't promise a grid-tie until the utility's application and this interface are actually sorted.

title: Simplified LV connection
summary: In short: a simpler connection path for small low-voltage generators. The utility still decides.
tip: Why it matters for us: ask the municipality or Eskom which path this site is on before the inverter is ordered.

title: Quality of supply
summary: In short: the NRS series on the quality of the power the utility delivers, and what a customer can expect.
tip: Why it matters for us: if the site complains about dips or flicker, this is the language the utility uses. Don't invent our own.

title: PV documentation and tests
summary: In short: the inspection, test, and paperwork set for a grid-connected PV system.
tip: Why it matters for us: write the sheets while you are still on the roof. Memory is a bad commissioning tool.

title: PV array design
summary: In short: design requirements for the array itself, not just hanging modules and hoping.
tip: Why it matters for us: size the strings before the cable is pulled. Reworking a finished string is a rotten afternoon.

title: PV module qualification
summary: In short: the design-qualification and type-approval tests for terrestrial PV modules.
tip: Why it matters for us: a module without a credible qualification is a gamble on the roof. Ask for it on the datasheet.

title: PV module safety
summary: In short: the safety qualification for PV modules, construction and fire behaviour included.
tip: Why it matters for us: qualification and safety are two different certificates. We want both before we buy a container of modules.

title: PV in the LV installation
summary: In short: low-voltage installation requirements aimed at a solar photovoltaic supply.
tip: Why it matters for us: the PV kit still has to live with the rest of the building's electrical install.

title: Protection against shock
summary: In short: the basic rules for keeping people from an electric shock in a low-voltage install.
tip: Why it matters for us: earthing, disconnection, and barriers are the shock plan. Don't leave a frame or a cabinet as an afterthought.

title: PV converter safety
summary: In short: safety requirements for the power converters used in PV systems, inverters included.
tip: Why it matters for us: an inverter without a credible safety listing does not go on a client roof.

title: Anti-islanding test method
summary: In short: the test procedure that checks a PV inverter stops feeding a grid that has gone dead.
tip: Why it matters for us: don't turn anti-islanding off to make commissioning easier. Someone may be working on that line.

title: Industrial lithium safety
summary: In short: safety requirements for lithium cells and batteries used in industrial applications, storage included.
tip: Why it matters for us: ask which cell standard is on the datasheet. A brochure is not a safety case.

title: Battery installation safety
summary: In short: the series on safe installation of secondary batteries, layout and protection included.
tip: Why it matters for us: ventilation, access, and isolation belong to the battery job, not the snag list.

title: Electrical energy storage
summary: In short: the IEC series for electrical energy storage systems, planning and the system itself.
tip: Why it matters for us: when a client says 'just a battery', this is the family of documents that treats it as a system.

title: Energy storage systems
summary: In short: a US listing for energy storage systems and equipment. Useful as a reference, not a SA law.
tip: Why it matters for us: if a cabinet claims a listing, check it is the system listing and not only a cell inside it.

title: Thermal runaway fire test
summary: In short: a test method for how a battery fire spreads. It is evidence, not a promise that a fire cannot start.
tip: Why it matters for us: ask for the test report when the room or the spacing is being argued. Don't invent the spacing.

title: Stationary storage installs
summary: In short: a US installation standard for stationary energy storage. Reference only, unless a spec calls it up.
tip: Why it matters for us: it is a useful checklist for siting and fire access. It does not replace the SA wiring code.

title: DER interconnection
summary: In short: the IEEE rules for connecting distributed resources to the power system. A reference, not our utility's NRS.
tip: Why it matters for us: inverter menus often speak IEEE. The job we hand over still has to satisfy NRS and the local utility.

title: UPS systems
summary: In short: the series for uninterruptible power systems, performance and how they are specified.
tip: Why it matters for us: a battery inverter that makes its own supply is not automatically a UPS. Read what the client actually bought.

title: Generating sets
summary: In short: the ISO series for engine-driven AC generating sets, ratings and performance.
tip: Why it matters for us: a genset nameplate rating is not the same as what it can do in our control scheme. Read the duty.

title: Rotating machines
summary: In short: the big series on rotating electrical machines, motors and generators.
tip: Why it matters for us: when we drive or protect a machine, the rating and the duty live here, not in a guess.

title: LV switchgear
summary: In short: low-voltage switchgear and controlgear. Breakers, contactors, and disconnectors live in this series.
tip: Why it matters for us: a device is only good for the duty on its label. Don't borrow an AC part for a DC job.

title: LV assemblies
summary: In short: requirements for low-voltage switchgear assemblies, the panel as a built product.
tip: Why it matters for us: a board we design and populate is an assembly. The parts being listed does not list the whole box.

title: IP ratings
summary: In short: the code for how well an enclosure keeps out dust and water. The two digits mean different things.
tip: Why it matters for us: an outdoor inverter or a roof box needs the rating the site actually throws at it. Don't read one digit and stop.

title: Surge protective devices
summary: In short: the series for low-voltage surge protective devices, selection and application included.
tip: Why it matters for us: PV and a long cable run are a lightning magnet. Put the SPD where the standard expects it, and bond it properly.

title: Lightning protection
summary: In short: the SA adoption of IEC 62305, protection against lightning for structures and the services on them.
tip: Why it matters for us: a roof full of metal and cable needs a lightning story. Modules and frames are not a substitute for one.

title: Hazardous areas
summary: In short: explosive atmospheres. Equipment and wiring in those areas follow this series.
tip: Why it matters for us: batteries, gensets, and fuel stores can create a zone. If the site is hazardous, ordinary gear does not go there.

title: Electromagnetic compatibility
summary: In short: the EMC series. How much a product may emit, and how much interference it must survive.
tip: Why it matters for us: a PLC that resets next to a drive is often an EMC problem. Route, screen, and earth before you blame the code.

title: Power electronic converters
summary: In short: safety requirements for power electronic converter systems, wider than PV inverters alone.
tip: Why it matters for us: storage converters and drives sit here too. Ask which safety standard the box was actually built to.

title: Utility automation comms
summary: In short: communication for substation and utility automation. A data model, not just a wire.
tip: Why it matters for us: if a protection or grid device speaks 61850, Modbus habits will not map it. Get the point list.

title: Telecontrol over TCP
summary: In short: telecontrol of remote gear over a standard network. Used by utilities more than by a small PLC.
tip: Why it matters for us: don't promise the municipality a 104 link unless we actually have the stack and the point list.

title: PLC general information
summary: In short: the overview of programmable controllers, what the family of standards is about.
tip: Why it matters for us: it is the front door. The language we write, and the tests the hardware survived, are the later parts.

title: PLC equipment requirements
summary: In short: equipment requirements and tests for the controller hardware itself.
tip: Why it matters for us: a cheap remote IO dropped in a hot panel may not have been built for that. Check the equipment rating.

title: PLC programming languages
summary: In short: the common PLC languages. Structured Text in PC Worx and PLCnext lives here.
tip: Why it matters for us: write ST the next person can read on a call-out. Clever one-liners are how plants stay down.

title: Control system security
summary: In short: security for industrial automation and control systems, zones and who may talk to whom.
tip: Why it matters for us: no default passwords, no surprise remote access, and the PLC does not sit on the guest Wi-Fi.

title: RS-485 electrical layer
summary: In short: the electrical spec for a balanced multipoint serial link. Modbus RTU usually rides on this.
tip: Why it matters for us: daisy chain it, terminate the two ends, and earth the shield in one place. It is not a star.

title: Modbus application protocol
summary: In short: the application protocol for registers and coils, over serial or TCP. The byte order is not settled by the spec alone.
tip: Why it matters for us: get the map from the device manual. The protocol tells you the frame, not what register 40001 means on that box.

title: Energy efficiency in buildings
summary: In short: energy-efficiency requirements for buildings in SA. It sits next to the building regulations.
tip: Why it matters for us: a PV or storage job can be pulled into the building's energy story. Know if the architect already has a target.

title: Building energy usage
summary: In short: the National Building Regulations part on energy usage in buildings.
tip: Why it matters for us: hot water, lighting, and the envelope are this document. Our plant does not replace it.

title: Safe work and the CoC
summary: In short: the occupational health and safety law. The electrical certificate says the install meets the wiring code.
tip: Why it matters for us: lock out, prove dead, and don't sign a certificate for work you did not inspect.

title: Regulator registration
summary: In short: the energy regulator. Some generation needs a licence or a registration. The size cutoff is not ours to invent.
tip: Why it matters for us: ask which approval this plant and this utility actually need before we run in parallel.

title: Modbus word and byte order
summary: In short: two boxes can read the same registers and still disagree which byte is the big one.
tip: Why it matters for us: check one known value, a serial or a voltage you can meter, before the map is trusted.

title: Scaling a register
summary: In short: the register is often a raw integer. The device manual says how that becomes a real unit.
tip: Why it matters for us: scale it in one place in the ST, then check it with a meter. Don't hide multipliers all over the program.

title: Cold-morning string voltage
summary: In short: a cold panel makes a higher open-circuit voltage than the sticker, which is at standard test conditions.
tip: Why it matters for us: size the string so a cold dawn still sits inside the inverter. A hot afternoon is the easy case.

title: Anti-islanding
summary: In short: if the grid dies, the inverter must stop pushing power, so a dead line stays dead.
tip: Why it matters for us: prove it drops out when the grid side is opened. A setting on a screen is not a test.

title: SOC and SOH
summary: In short: state of charge is how full it is now. State of health is how much capacity is left compared with new.
tip: Why it matters for us: a battery showing full can still be tired. Don't tell the client charge and pretend it is health.

title: C-rate
summary: In short: how hard you push the battery compared with its capacity. Faster usually means hotter and a shorter life.
tip: Why it matters for us: stay inside the charge and discharge rates the manufacturer published. Don't just try a bigger number.

title: Peak shaving
summary: In short: use the battery so the site does not set a new maximum demand. The demand charge remembers the peak.
tip: Why it matters for us: agree the ceiling with the client and alarm before it is hit. After the peak, the bill is already written.

title: Time-of-use arbitrage
summary: In short: charge when energy is cheap, and use the battery when it is expensive.
tip: Why it matters for us: put the tariff seasons where someone can see them in the PLC. A wrong season quietly costs money.
